 Follow Republican Rep. James Comer enters 2027 Kentucky governor's race
 Lucas Aulbach, Louisville Courier Journal Updated Tue, November 17, 2026 at 12:04 AM UTC 4 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. U.S. Rep. James Comer is making a second run for governor – and this time, he's the clear front-runner among Kentucky Republicans.
 Comer, who's been in Congress since late 2016 , announced he plans to run for the commonwealth's highest elected office. The well-known 54-year-old Republican lawmaker made his plans official in a Nov. 16 announcement on his campaign website , where he took questions from some listeners.
 "Kentucky needs a leader whose policies will lead to growth and good-paying jobs. We need a leader whose priority will be to reduce taxes so Kentuckians can keep more of what they earn," Comer said. "The government doesn't have all the answers, but we have a responsibility to solve problems and lift people up when we can."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While a few other registered Republicans have filed paperwork with the Kentucky Registry of Election Finance indicating they plan to run for governor, Comer is by far the biggest GOP name in the race to this point.
 You can expect him to have significant party backing, as well. Secretary of State Michael Adams and Agriculture Commissioner Jonathan Shell have openly encouraged him to run and called on others to support him, and a number of other elected Republicans and powerful party figures are also expected to endorse him.
 "I love this environment," said U.S. Rep. James Comer said about the political barbs thrown during the Fancy Farm speeches. "It's like a regular House Oversight Committee meeting."
Comer spoke at St. Jerome Catholic Church Fancy Farm Picnic Saturday August 2, 2025 in Fancy Farm, Kentucky. Two Democrats are currently running in the 2027 primary: Rocky Adkins, a longtime former state House leader who served as Gov. Andy Beshear's senior adviser for more than six years; and Lt. Gov. Jacqueline Coleman, who's been lieutenant governor throughout Beshear's time in office.
 Comer vs. the field
 Three other Republicans – Rick Hardin of Leitchfield, Brett St. Amand of Lexington and Charles "Bruiser" Martin of London – have indicated in KREF filings that they plan to run for governor.
 Advertisement Advertisement None have a fraction of the name identification that Comer brings, though. And many Republicans around the state in recent years have made it clear they plan to support the congressman should he seek to return to Frankfort. Comer may have cleared much of the GOP field just by launching his campaign.
 Adams, the term-limited secretary of state who won more votes than any statewide candidate on the ballot in 2023, won't be in the race. After teasing for months that he may run, Adams took the stage at the Fancy Farm political picnic in August and announced he would instead stay out of it and support Comer , urging attendees to "unite right now" behind the GOP's "strongest candidate."
 Attorney General Russell Coleman in August told The Courier Journal he'll support Comer if he runs, and Shell has gone out of his way several times over the past year to tout Comer, who was Kentucky's agriculture commissioner for four years before entering Congress.
 "I'll be his biggest advocate, his largest vocal supporter," Shell told The Courier Journal in an August interview. "We need his leadership in Frankfort. He has a vision for the state of Kentucky."
 Advertisement Advertisement U.S. Rep. Brett Guthrie told reporters at a Nov. 2 event that he would support his fellow congressman if he entered the race. "Kentucky couldn't have a better governor than Jamie Comer," he said.

Aug. 1, 2026 (Scott Utterback/Courier Journal) Comer's credentials
 Comer, a Western Kentucky University graduate raised in Tompkinsville, has a lengthy history in Kentucky politics.
 He served as a state representative from 2001-11 before being elected agriculture commissioner. He held that job for one four-year term before launching a campaign for governor in 2014, with state Sen. Chris McDaniel joining him on the ticket as lieutenant governor for the 2015 election.
 The Republican primary, where he faced businessman and former U.S. Senate candidate Matt Bevin and ex-Louisville Metro Council member Hal Heiner, was close. Comer eventually fell to Bevin by just 83 votes after a former girlfriend told The Courier Journal in a letter that he had been physically and mentally abusive to her during their two-year relationship. Comer vehemently denied those claims , reported weeks before the primary.
 Advertisement Advertisement Comer won a congressional race a year later to replace 1st Congressional District Rep. Ed Whitfield, who resigned late in his term. He's held that position since then and eventually was named chair of the powerful House Oversight Committee, where he's led investigations into the federal government's probe of sex trafficking allegations against Jeffrey Epstein, as well as claims Hunter Biden, the son of former President Joe Biden, improperly used his family connections for personal gain.
 Kentucky's 2027 primary elections will take place on May 18, with the general election set for Nov. 2.
